This modest initial wet weight stands in contrast to the ultimate size attained by adult females, which reach an asymptotic body mass of 76.5 grams [Wwi = 76.5 grams], with a documented range of 68 to 85 grams across multiple populations in northern Thailand and southern China. The nestling phase is intensive, with both parents provisioning the developing chicks through a combination of insect prey and tree sap.

The value is consistent with allometric predictions for a picid of this body mass, falling within the range reported for other woodpecker species such as Dendrocopos major and Picus canus. The relatively high metabolic rate may reflect the energetic costs associated with the species' active foraging strategy, which involves sustained climbing, clinging, and percussive drilling on hard bamboo surfaces.
